newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Wall St bull runs again, Euro-shares follow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wall St bull runs again, Euro-shares follow.

text.p: European shares charged higher in early trade on Thursday after Wall Street put a week of declines behind it and surged overnight, while the dollar held steady.
"The Dow's raging bull may be back on track," the head of share trading at a large investment bank in London said. "People will be pretty confident now -- until Wall Street falls again."

London's FTSE 100 index was up 19.8 points, or 0.47 percent, at 4,227.4 by 1000 GMT, while in Paris the CAC 40 index was up 29.81 points, or 1.21 percent, at 2,494.82. In Frankfurt the DAX was up 19.23 points, or 0.64 percent, at 3,018.43.

In New York on Wednesday the Dow industrials average, which had fallen during the previous five sessions, closed 84.66 points higher at 6,740.74, its best gain since January 3 when it surged 102 points.

But gains in the broader U.S. share markets were negligible and U.S. analysts said the market's extreme volatility, a growing worry, had prompted investors to seek the relative safety of big-name blue-chip stocks.

Volatility was the watchword in Tokyo, too, where the key Nikkei average ended with a loss of 2.57 percent, or just over 471 points. it gave back almost half of the gains racked up in the previous two sessions.
European dealers said participants on both sides of the Atlantic would remain cautious ahead of next week's U.S. Federal Reserve regular monetary meeting, which could change U.S. interest rates.
While most economists do not expect the Fed to push up U.S. rates, some believe signs of a robust U.S. economy will lead to a tightening sooner rather than later.
HIgher interest rates would sorely test the world's share markets, many of which are at or near record levels, by making returns on alternative investments and cash more attractive.
French shares were particularly strong, hitting a record high, surpassing the previous peak set on Tuesday.

"The (corporate) results have been taken very well, Wall St looks good, the dollar's holding, there's growth without inflation in the U.S. and there's a chance of lower rates in France: What more could you ask for?" a Paris trader said.
The market, however, was not really expecting a cut in the intervention rate after Thursday's French monetary council meeting.

Alcatel Alsthom surged as much as 7.6 percent to a high of 487.0 francs after it said it expected a net profit of some 2.5 billion francs for 1996 following one of the worst French corporate losses in 1995. It's year high is 500. German shares advanced in early bourse dealings, catching up with IBIS computer trade gains tied to Wall Street's gains and a the steady dollar.
Allianz was up sharply after Goldman Sachs confirmed it had re-rated the insurance group to a market outperformer.

In currencies, the dollar was steady in European morning trade, though its tone on the yen was muted by the Japanese Finance Ministry's reported comment that Tokyo will intervene in the market when the timing makes it effective.
While his remark was not expected to drive down the dollar any more during the day, the market would use it as a chance to settle down after the dollar's recent hectic moves, analysts said.

"Basically these comments were a gentle reminder to the market not to get carried away, and that the bottom line is that the Bank of Japan will intervene if the market becomes disorderly," said UBS senior currency economist Paul Lambert.

"The further it gets above 120 yen, the more investors are going to become nervous about Japanese authorities' intervention, although we haven't seen any evidence of that yet," said Don Smith, international economist at HSBC Markets.
Against the mark, the dollar was expected to drift sideways due to a lack of fresh incentives.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6427 marks and 121.70 yen compared with late Wednesday's European levels of 1.6428 marks and 121.99 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was up 19.9 points, or 0.47 percent, at 4,227.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 29.81 points, or 1.21 percent, at 2,494.82.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 19.23 points, or 0.64 percent, at 3,018.43.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened weaker at $349.55 after closing on Wednesday at $351.05.
